text:
Alex: Quick heads-up — I'm proposing we flip VPC egress posture in privnet to a cascading-deny by default for non-control subnets. Goal: shrink audit surface and block accidental outbound. Risk: keystore/KMS calls and NAT-fallbacking warm pools might fail provisioning and spike errors.
Meera: If you mean drop-all-by-default + explicit allows for privatelink/keystore, we need a short-lived exception for the keystore SG. Warm pools call keystore via privatelink but older nodes fall back to NAT; they also pull AMIs from S3 occasionally.
Jordan: We saw this last month in staging when a tight rule landed — keystore decrypt errors jumped. Snippet from staging logs: 
```
2026-02-12T08:41:22Z node-ct-12 keystore: decrypt err: timeout dial tcp 10.10.5.3:443 i/o timeout
2026-02-12T08:41:28Z node-ct-12 provision: warmpool failure: 504 gateway timeout
```
Liz: Cost angle — allowing temporary NAT egress vs. increasing flow log retention. Which is cheaper if we need a 6h emergency window? We should model both.
Ryan: Back-of-envelope: at 120 qps decrypt traffic * 3KB/request => ~31GB/day ~ $0.8/day per NAT in eu-west-2. If retries cause 3x traffic that gets non-trivial but still < $10/day. Flow logs retention is trickier (ingest price + S3/ELK storage).
Meera: Mitigation proposal: (1) create tag-based SG exception limited to keystore prefix-lists + privatelink endpoints, (2) prefer privatelink route policy, (3) deploy a tiny canary warm pool in eu-west with verbose logging and higher sampling.
Alex: Operational plan idea: short-lived allowlist on `sg-keystore-XXXX` for up to 6 hours while we rollout a targeted rule set. Steps: create rule, run canary 2h, monitor `keystore.decrypt.*` and `gpu.provision.latency`. Revert if regressions.
OpsBot: Alert: keystore.decrypt.errors increased x7 over baseline in prod-eu at 2026-02-11T18:02:09Z — correlated with firewall tighten event (event-id: fw-20260211-18).
Jordan: +1 to canary. Also bump Flow Log sampling on affected subnets for 12h (sample_rate 1% -> 10%) so we can trace dropped connections without keeping full retention.
Liz: Runbook snippet to include in rollout doc:
```
- create sg-exception tag: key=rbac:egress-exception value=keystore
- apply to privnet subnets (a,b) only
- bump flow log sample_rate=1% -> 10% for 12h
- monitor metrics: keystore.decrypt.errors, gpu.warmpool.success, provision.latency
- revert allowlist after 6h if no regressions or extend with approval
```
Alex: I'll open a small PR and schedule the canary for 16:00 UTC. Who owns monitoring + revert?
Jordan: I'll own monitoring. Will post grafana panels and add slack alert thresholds (keystore.decrypt.errors > 5/min triggers).
Meera: I'll own the PR + tag creation. Will coordinate with infra to reserve NAT capacity and a transient NAT route in case privatelink flaps.
Liz: I'll run the cost calc and post numbers in this thread by EOD. Short note: if we keep 10% flow sampling for 12h across 3 subnets, storage delta ~2GB compressed -> cheap.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: sg-exception-creat (staging) — scheduled 15:30 UTC.
Alex: Thanks all. Keep it tight; we can't loosen egress widely without audit visibility. Will add a short checklist to the PR with rollback commands and a contact list. :lock:
